text:
anna (support): FYI got an urgent ticket from AcmeCorp — p99s for /v1/embeddings spiked ~3x since Friday, some timeouts/504s. they say no code changes on their side. <https://support.acmecorp.tickets/REDACTED>

mike (sre): saw the alert and an uptick in SLA pages. which region?

anna (support): eu-west-1, mostly embed routes. p99 from ~1.2s -> ~4.5s, p95 ~2x. customer is pretty upset.

jordan (runtime): any infra deployments Friday morning? we rolled host kernel + CUDA13 driver in eu-west-1 then. could be related.

taylor (infra): yes — kernel 6.6 + NV driver 535 went out friday. preliminary metrics show hostfs iowait spikes when kv-cache flushes coincide with GPU DMA. might be qdepth saturation.

mike (sre): can someone paste `iostat -x 1 3` from an affected host?

taylor (infra): here's a snippet from node-42 during a tail spike:

```
avg-cpu:  %user   %system  %iowait
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         320.0   40.0  15000  2000   44.0     25.6   0.80   85.2
```

jordan (runtime): 85% util and await ~25ms — that will amplify token tail latencies. our kv-cache writes + eviction churn likely create bursts of hostfs IO at critical moments.

mike (sre): immediate mitigations we should try: 1) route AcmeCorp traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1, 2) increase disk qdepth / tune nvme scheduler on affected nodes, 3) smooth kv-cache flush batches to avoid spikes. can we do 1+2 quickly?

taylor (infra): starting qdepth bump and enabling per-node write coalescing. will drain two nodes to apply safely. ETA ~12m.

anna (support): told customer we're investigating and offered temporary reroute + ETA.

ops-bot: Deploy started — rolling change: /etc/nvme/qdepth adjusted on nodes [node-42, node-43].

jordan (runtime): I'll prepare a fallback policy to use a smaller model variant (less kv-cache pressure) and add a circuit-breaker for p99>2s over 10m for AcmeCorp.

taylor (infra): qdepth change applied to node-42, node-43. iowait dropped to ~6ms immediately on those hosts. monitoring ingress.

mike (sre): good. can we run a driver rollback on a spare host to validate driver/kernel interaction hypothesis before broader action?

taylor (infra): staging driver rollback on test-host-01 now and running loadgen against the embed endpoint.

anna (support): customer reports latency improving for many requests :thumbsup:, still occasionally seeing tails. asking for ETA on full fix.

jordan (runtime): sample stalled request captured in logs:

```
req_id=abc123 start=0 hostfs_wait=24.8ms gpu_stall=3.2ms kv_write=19.5ms total=4.8s
```

(tells the story: hostfs_wait + kv_write dominate tail)

taylor (infra): rollback on test-host-01 completed — under synthetic load p99 dropped ~60% vs post-rollforward. points to driver+firmware+kernel interaction increasing hostfs latency under concurrent GPU DMA.

mike (sre): action plan: 1) widen routing so AcmeCorp traffic serves from eu-central-1 while we stabilize, 2) canary driver rollback to a small subset of eu-west-1 hosts, 3) coordinate with kernel team/vendor for patch or vendor driver fix, 4) run preprod storage-profile regression tests, 5) postmortem + customer RCA.

anna (support): noted and communicated plan to customer. ticket INC-2026-ACME assigned.

ops-bot: Route change applied for customer AcmeCorp -> eu-central-1.

mike (sre): owners: taylor (infra) lead for infra rollback, jordan (runtime) for fallback routing/circuit-breaker, anna (support) customer comms. follow-up sync in 30m.

anna (support): thanks — keeping customer updated, will escalate to execs if tails persist.
